content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Change-aware pipelines can identify modified components, but they must account for shared dependencies and ensure a filter cannot bypass required checks. Enterprise design requires consistent policy, explicit ownership, auditable privilege boundaries, reviewed shared workflows, controlled artifact promotion, and documented recovery. The most useful check is one that produces observable evidence and fails clearly when its stated requirement is not met.

items.title: Detecting changed files
items.text: For detecting changed files, state the expected input and result, identify the relevant workflow field or operational decision, and verify it with a controlled check plus run logs. Document the failure condition rather than relying on the YAML file merely parsing.

items.title: Identifying affected project components
items.text: For identifying affected project components, state the expected input and result, identify the relevant workflow field or operational decision, and verify it with a controlled check plus run logs. Document the failure condition rather than relying on the YAML file merely parsing.

items.title: Dynamic matrix generation
items.text: List the supported combinations explicitly and use `include`/`exclude` or `max-parallel` to control expansion. Keep all required configurations covered and avoid unnecessary duplicate jobs.

items.title: Monorepo dependency relationships
items.text: Declare job dependencies with `needs` and read prerequisite results or outputs through `needs.<job>`. Separate jobs do not share a runner workspace automatically.

items.title: Avoiding incorrect skipped checks
items.text: For avoiding incorrect skipped checks, state the expected input and result, identify the relevant workflow field or operational decision, and verify it with a controlled check plus run logs. Document the failure condition rather than relying on the YAML file merely parsing.

items.title: Testing shared code used by multiple components
items.text: Make the check deterministic and fail with a meaningful status when requirements are not met. Preserve reports where useful and configure required branch checks to match the checks the workflow actually emits.

content_blocks.code:
name: Selective component checks
on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - "services/api/**"
      - "shared/**"
      - "pyproject.toml"
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  api-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: echo "Run API tests when API or shared dependencies change"
content_blocks.expected_output: The path filter includes both the API and shared dependency locations; update it when the component dependency graph changes.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Test API, shared-library, and unrelated-file changes in a sandbox and verify that required checks still run for relevant edits.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Do not use a narrow path filter that silently skips validation of shared code.

content_blocks.title: Practice and verification
content_blocks.text: Inspect the example and make one focused change related to change detection and selective pipelines. Predict the expected result first, then use the run instructions or a static review to check it. Record the difference between your prediction and the actual result. Do not add production secrets or grant write permissions just to make a sample pass.

items.title: Syntax and scope
items.text: Check YAML indentation and confirm whether the setting belongs at workflow, job, or step level.

items.title: Permissions and trust
items.text: Start with read-only access. If the example needs more access, explain the exact operation and reduce permissions again afterwards.

items.title: Evidence
items.text: Use the run summary and first failing step. A green result is meaningful only when the intended checks actually ran.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: You should now be able to explain change detection and selective pipelines, read the example, and identify a way to validate it. The wider system goal remains: Standardize workflow behavior across teams without hiding important security boundaries.

content.task: Apply change detection and selective pipelines to a small workflow change. State the expected result first, validate the configuration, then record evidence from the run or static check.
task_acceptance_criteria: Identify the relevant event, workflow field, runner behavior, or security boundary.
Explain the expected success result and at least one failure or skip condition.
Use least privilege and a disposable/test context; do not include credentials or production resources.

content.expected_output: The expected result is the behavior described here: Change-aware pipelines can identify modified components, but they must account for shared dependencies and ensure a filter cannot bypass required checks. The real result depends on the repository, selected ref, configured permissions, and runner availability.
troubleshooting: If a workflow never starts, verify the workflow is under `.github/workflows/`, the event and filters match, and repository/organization Actions policy allows it.
If a step fails, inspect the first failed step, exit code, stderr, installed tool versions, permissions, and runner/network state before retrying.
If a job is skipped or data is missing, inspect `if`, `needs`, outputs, artifact names/paths, and cache keys; jobs do not automatically share filesystems.
common_mistakes: Assuming YAML parsing proves the workflow runs correctly or matches the intended trigger.
Granting broad token permissions, printing environment values, or exposing a secret to untrusted code.
Using a placeholder command as evidence of a real build, test, deployment, or security scan.
